updated 30 October 2026 · metagame window: Space Marines codex and Power Armour update: 3 Oct to 16 Oct

40k 11th edition: faction balance

Strike Force (2000 pts) games from 3 October to 16 October: 12,165 matches from 352 events, 6,888 lists. The first player wins 51.8%.

This metagame window

This page covers games played from 3 October to 16 October, the period between two milestones. Every figure, ranking and comparison on it uses only those games. The whole-edition page and the other windows are in the window menu at the top. How the window began, with a before and after comparison, is under the milestone of 3 October on the whole-edition page.

Summary

Units

The median faction has 6 units in at least half of its lists and 25 in at least 10%. 17% of current datasheets (191 of 1,140) were never played or appeared in under 1% of lists. Of 540 units in 40 or more lists, 5 (1%) have a clear effect on results, 1 positive and 4 negative. Those units are picked less often than others: the median share of lists is 12%, against 36% for all units.

Detachments

The median faction needs 4 detachments to cover 80% of its lists, and 11 factions have one detachment in at least half of its lists. Of 9 detachments in 150 or more lists, 1 (11%) differ from their own faction's average. That is a higher share than for units (1%) or combinations (3%), so detachment choice is the largest source of imbalance inside a faction.

Combinations

68% of lists run two or more detachments. Of 98 setups (combinations plus single 3-point detachments) in 15 or more lists, 3 differ from the faction average (2 better, 1 worse). The strongest is Assault Brethren + Deathwatch Support + Terminator Storm Force in Space Marines (22.1 points above the faction average), the weakest Hunting Warpack + Traitoris Lance in Chaos Knights (14.7 points below the faction average).

Time and milestones

No factions of 28 have a clearly different win rate in the latest period than in the first. 0% of detachments and 0% of units (with 25 or more lists) changed their share of lists by at least 8 points, with a clear margin, between the first period and the last 28 days. Each faction section lists the biggest changes.

Milestones

Data in this window starts on 3 October and runs to 16 October. Weekly games went from 8,204 in the first full week to 13,646 in the week of 5 October. no milestones are marked below. Effects are measured as the 28 days before against the 28 days after each date.

No milestone falls inside this window, so the games below describe one steady metagame. The effect of the milestone that opened the window is in the whole-edition page and in the window before this one.

How to read the tables

Adjusted for player skill

A faction's win rate also reflects who plays it. To separate the two, one model on 12,109 games gives every faction and every player a strength. It then estimates what each faction wins against the opponents it actually met when both players are average and nobody goes first. 59% of the games have a player who appears in five or more games, so skill is known well for experienced players and is pulled toward average for the rest. The adjustment still improves predictions on events the model has not seen, so it carries real information.

The adjustment is modest and widens the gaps. The largest changes are Imperial Agents (3.4 points down), Astra Militarum (2.8 points down) and Genestealer Cult (2.2 points down), and 15 factions change place in the ranking. Strong factions move up and weak ones down because their opponents tend to be stronger players: Swiss pairings match winning players against each other, so a faction that wins a lot meets better opposition in later rounds. The own-players column shows how much better or worse than average the faction's own players are, the opponents column the same for the players they met, both as the win rate against an average player.

How to read the tables

High-rated games

The metagame among the best players can differ from the aggregate. Every player gets a rating that is updated after each game, using only earlier games. A game counts as high-rated when both players have played at least 5 earlier games and both ratings are in the top 25% or the top 10% of rated players. That leaves 44 games in the top 25% and 12 in the top 10%, out of 12,109 games, so the tables below are noisier than the season figures. Ratings are built from this season's games only, so they follow recent form more than a long career. The rating predicts the winner in 53% of games between rated players, which is enough to separate strong from average players but not to rank neighbours.

Compared with all games, the share of games rises most for Space Marines (13.0 points), Leagues of Votann (5.9 points) and Orks (3.8 points) in the top 25% and falls most for Adeptus Custodes (4.6 points), Death Guard (3.7 points) and Dark Angels (3.6 points). Win rates are for games between different factions; a faction needs 40 games in a subset to get a figure. Intervals are 95% ranges.

How to read the tables

Emperor's Children, Chaos Knights, Grey Knights, Adeptus Custodes and World Eaters play from the smallest pool of units (effective unit count 15 to 19), while Space Marines, Space Wolves and Astra Militarum have the widest (73 for the broadest). Across factions the correlation between effective unit count and win rate is -0.01. The narrowest factions include both strong and weak ones.

In 11 factions a single detachment is in at least half of all lists: Imperial Agents (Veiled Blade Elimination Force, 100%), Adeptus Mechanicus (Cohort Cybernetica, 75%), World Eaters (Berzerker Warband, 70%), Adeptus Custodes (Lions of the Emperor, 67%), Leagues of Votann (Hearthguard Covenant, 62%), Deathwatch (Black Spear Task Force, 61%), Blood Angels (Assault Brethren, 60%), Space Wolves (Saga of the Great Wolf, 58%), Drukhari (Exhibition of Slaughter, 57%), Chaos Knights (Hunting Warpack, 56%) and Black Templars (Assault Brethren, 55%).

109 of 1,140 current datasheets never appeared in a Strike Force list, and 82 more appeared in under 1% of their faction's lists. The factions with the most unused datasheets: Genestealer Cult (24 never, 0 rare), Aeldari (13 never, 8 rare), Chaos Daemons (10 never, 5 rare) and Adeptus Custodes (7 never, 8 rare).

Extra areas

Force Disposition against Force Disposition

11,889 games had a known Force Disposition on both sides. The same choice met itself in 23.5% of them; draws were 3.3% of all games.

No pairing has a clear edge: every result is close to an even split once the number of games is taken into account.

Draws are most common in Disruption against itself (8.9% of 123 games) and least common in Priority Assets against Purge the Foe (1.8% of 1,312).

List width

Lists were ranked by the number of distinct unit types within each faction and split into four equal groups, using only lists whose parsed unit points add up to at least 1,850. Lists with fewer distinct units have a higher win rate: +2.4 points in the group with the fewest against -4.6 in the group with the most.

Multiple copies of the same unit

For units that appear both as a single copy and as two or more copies in at least 50 lists each, taking multiples gives a higher win rate for Malignant Plaguecaster (Death Guard, 19.9 points above single-copy lists), Redemptor Dreadnought (Space Marines, 18.2 points above single-copy lists) and Myphitic Blight-hauler (Death Guard, 17.8 points above single-copy lists) and lower for . The comparison does not adjust for what else is in the list.

Player base

Dropping each faction's three most active players changes its win rate by less than 1 point in 24 of 28 factions. The exceptions are Imperial Agents (-8.4 points, five most active players = 42% of games), Imperial Knights (-1.2 points, five most active players = 6% of games), Genestealer Cult (-1.1 points, five most active players = 13% of games) and Drukhari (-1.0 points, five most active players = 9% of games). The skill proxy (each player's results at their other events) differs little between factions, from -0.4 to +1.8 points, so player track record does not explain the ranking.

Method

Data

24,330 player-game rows (12,165 matches) from 352 events in Strike Force (2000 pts) format. Mirror matches count once and draws count 0.5. The data holds 6,888 lists from 28 factions.

Effects

Each game result is compared with a prediction from the two factions' strength and the first-turn effect. A list's effect is its average result minus that prediction. Item effects (units, detachments, combinations, enhancements, Force Disposition) are group averages of these list results, with standard errors clustered by list. Detachment effects are measured against the faction average. Combination effects include the strength of the detachments in them. Enhancement effects are measured against other lists with the same detachment. Unit effects are measured against lists with the same detachment strength and the same number of distinct units. Shrinkage towards the faction mean is used only to rank noisy items.

An effect is called clear when it is at least 3 standard errors from zero and also passes a false discovery check. Units, detachments, enhancements and combinations are tested in four groups (958 items in all), and within each group the expected share of false findings among the clear ones is held at 5%. That check removed 9 items that would otherwise have been called clear. A single borderline item should still be read with care. Items in fewer than 15 to 40 lists, depending on the table, are left out.

Player track record

Each player's average result at their other events (leave-one-event-out, shrunk towards zero) is subtracted. About 11% of games have such a history. Players with a single event get no adjustment.

Parse completeness

The parser reads the unit points of nearly every list: the average sum of parsed unit points is about 1,988 of 2,000, and 97.0% of lists reach 1,950 or more. Lists with fewer parsed points have a different win rate by up to about 56 points between the lowest and highest groups, and results were adjusted for this before items were compared. The list-width table uses only lists with at least 1,850 parsed points. Pick rates are shares of all lists in the faction. Faction, matchup and detachment results are not affected (detachment effects correlate 1.00 with the unadjusted values).

Strong players against the rest

Each faction section and each milestone compares players in the top 25% and top 10% by rating with all other players. A list belongs to the group its player was in before the list's first game, and unrated players count as other players. Win rates use only games where both players are in the same group, so a strong player is never compared with a weak opponent: 44 games between two top 25% players, 12 between two top 10% players and 11,868 between two other players, with 197 mixed games left out. Around milestones the comparison is made on share of lists, because games between strong players are too few to split by date. Differences in detachments, units and enhancements need a clear margin and at least 5 points to be shown, since many items are compared at once.

Detachment completeness

A list has three Detachment Points to spend, and each detachment costs one to three. 9% of the lists in this report (636 of 6,888) name detachments that add up to less than the list's budget, mostly because the list text names only one. Lists where exactly one more detachment fits the gap and is named in the list header or implied by its enhancements were completed before the analysis. The rest are kept as they are, so detachment shares and combinations are slightly understated for the factions with the largest gaps. Point costs of detachments change with rules updates, so each list is read with the cost that applied on the day of its event.

Limits

Results show what happens in tournaments. Players choose what to bring, and those choices follow skill, preparation and the opponents they expect. Points and rules changed during the period, and milestones fall close together, so a change after a milestone does not prove a single cause. Effects are associations. Small factions such as Deathwatch and Imperial Agents have wide uncertainty throughout, and all milestones have at least 14 days of data.

Results brackets use event standings from individual Strike Force events with at least 5 rounds only, a smaller set than the game-level analysis. Swiss pairing makes players with equal records meet, which compresses records, and strong players choose strong factions, so brackets reflect players as well as factions. Lists that did not play every round count as entries for X to X-2 but not for the win bands. Team events are included in all faction results; teams choose their own pairings, so the team events block of each faction sets them against its individual events. The charts in the milestone blocks use plain averages for that window without adjustment for opponent strength or list completeness. A dot is the win rate and the line is its 95% interval; a dot is coloured when the whole interval lies above or below the window's own win rate.

How to read the tables

Win rate
A win counts 1 and a draw 0.5. The 95% CI is the interval the true win rate lies in with 95% confidence.
Effect (pp)
The difference in win rate, in percentage points, between lists that include an item and comparable lists of the same faction, after allowing for opponent strength, the first-turn effect and the player's track record. The figure after the sign is one standard error.
z
The effect divided by its standard error. Values of 3 or more in either direction are called clear and coloured: blue for better, orange for worse. Units, detachments, enhancements and combinations must also pass a false discovery check, so a few colours are left out.
Model expects, Diff (pp), Reading
Model expects is the win rate predicted from both factions' strength and the first-turn effect. Diff is the gap between the actual win rate and that prediction. Reading is shown when the interval excludes 50% or the gap to the model is clear after multiple-testing control.
Lists, Pick, In % of lists
The number of lists containing the item and their share of the faction's lists. A list with two detachments counts for both.
P1 to P4
The share of the faction's lists that include the detachment in each period. The period dates are given in the Over time table of each faction.
Milestone table
Win rate and share of games in the 28 days before and after the milestone. Changes with z of 3 or more are coloured.
Effective units
The number of equally common units that would give the same spread of play; higher means more varied. It can exceed a faction's own datasheet count because lists also contain units from outside the faction's codex.
Avg list overlap
The average share of units two random lists of the faction have in common.
Results brackets
Win bands place each player by the share of games won (a draw counts half) among players who played every round. X is the most wins in the event; X, X-1 and X-2 count the lists with that many wins. Share of tier is the faction's share of the lists in that tier, share of entries its share of all lists entered, and ratio the first divided by the second.
Top-10% ratio
The faction's share of top-10% finishes divided by its share of entrants.
Pick-rate shifts
Share of the faction's lists that include the item in the first period, the 28 days before the last 28, and the last 28 days. Only changes of 4 or more standard errors and a sizeable gap are listed.

Units

A typical list contains 11 distinct units. 3 units appear in at least half of all lists and 34 in at least 10%. The most common is Gretchin (91% of lists). 4 datasheets never appeared: Burna Boyz, Grot Tanks, Lootas, Warboss on Warbike. 5 datasheets appeared in under 1% of lists: Blitza-bommer, Burna-bommer, Dakkajet, Kaptin Badrukk, Kill Tank.

Of 39 units in 40 or more lists, 1 has a clear effect on results (0 positive, 1 negative). Weakest: Deff Dread (12.7 points below comparable lists, 12% of lists).
